name: The five vows (Tattvārtha 7.1-7.8)
method_summary: Abstention from violence, falsehood, stealing, unchastity and possessiveness, in part (small vow) or wholly (great vow); five contemplations for each, for steadiness.

name: The contemplations for steadiness of the vows (Tattvārtha 7.4-7.8)
method_summary: For non-violence: restraint of speech and mind, careful walking, careful handling, looking at food and drink; for truthfulness: giving up anger, greed, fear, laughter and speaking in conformity; for non-stealing: empty and abandoned dwellings, not obstructing others, pure alms, no dispute with co-religionists; for chastity: giving up talk and sight that awaken attachment, recalling past enjoyment, stimulating foods and adorning the body; for non-possession: giving up attachment and aversion towards pleasant and unpleasant objects of the senses.

name: Reflection for dread of saṃsāra and detachment (Tattvārtha 7.9-7.12)
method_summary: Seeing danger and blame in violence and the other faults in this world and the next, or seeing them as suffering alone; reflecting on the nature of the world and body, for dread of saṃsāra and detachment.

name: Friendliness, delight, compassion and equanimity (Tattvārtha 7.11)
method_summary: Friendliness towards all living beings, delight in those superior in virtue, compassion for the afflicted and equanimity towards the undisciplined.
